newsitem.title: UK: UK budget to push up RPI index-ONS.
newsitem.headline: UK budget to push up RPI index-ONS.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics said on Tuesday that measures unveiled in Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first budget last week would have an upward effect of 0.79 percentage points on the monthly all-items UK RPI index.
But with the budget changes kicking in at different times, the full effect will not be felt until after April 1998 and the ONS estimates assume all tax and duty changes are passed on in full.
The impact of changes to excise duties will have an upward effect of 0.72 percentage points on the index.
Within that, alcohol will have an upward effect of 0.24 percentage points from January 1998 while tobacco will have an upward effect of 0.22 from December this year.

The increase in petrol prices is estimated to have an upward impact of 0.24 percentage points from July and vehicle excise duties is estimated to push the index up by 0.2 percentage points from December.
A reduction in VAT on heating on fuel will have a downward effect of 0.11 percentage points from September.

The abolition of the gas levy will have a downward effect of 0.03 percentage points from April 1998 while reduction in mortgage tax relief is estimated to have an upward effect of 0.21 percentage points in the same month..
The total one month effect of the November 1996 budget was 0.39 percentage points.

The budget changes will have a cumulative effect on the 12-month headline RPI rate. In July, the annual rate will be pushed up by 0.24 percentage points, assuming all changes are fully passed on, the ONS said.

In September, the 12-month rate should be forced up by 0.13 percentage points. In January next year, a 0.25 percentage point upward effect is estimated while in April, the 12-month rate would be forced up by 0.40 percentage points.
